packageRules.description: Maven: every dependency is a chore(deps) unless it reaches the consumer's classpath
Maven runtime-scope (compile and runtime) dependencies are fix(deps), i.e. patch releases
Non-major updates are grouped and raised weekly
Surefire and Failsafe move in one PR: since 3.6.x, -DskipTests changes how it affects Failsafe, and a lone bump breaks the JaCoCo check
Kotlin compiler and KotlinPoet updates go as one group, so the Kotlin toolchain and the generator's KotlinPoet dependency stay in step
JavaParser, compile-testing and ArchUnit each get their own PR: each is a large version jump
Majors stay in their own PRs, never grouped
PIT, JaCoCo and the Sonar scanner each get their own PR

JUnit Jupiter, the Platform launcher and the Gradle example's junit-bom share one version line; a lone bump leaves mismatched jars on the surefire classpath (#243, #255), so they move in one PR. Majors included: this rule comes after the major rule and overrides its groupName null for these packages

The frozen 5.x compatibility suite keeps its own pom unchanged (tree hash guard, docs/agents/5x-compatibility.md); Renovate must not touch it. The runner's pom is disabled too: its annotations 13.0 must equal the suite's, and automerge would bump only one of the two. The root dependencyManagement entry is still updated
The Gradle example's own artifacts follow the release (release-please bumps its version), not Renovate; its wrapper is a normal gradle-wrapper update
The latest CI leg follows the newest GA JDK, not only LTS releases; compare by major version only

customManagers.description: JDK version of the newest-GA leg in the CI verify matrix (role: latest)
